name: Bill Gates
title: Code for a Machine He'd Never Seen
subtitle: From a school teletype in Seattle to Microsoft, a $118 billion fortune, and a promise to give almost all of it away by 2045.
hook: Bill Gates has put an end date on his own fortune. On ==8 May 2025== he wrote that he will give away virtually all his wealth through the Gates Foundation, which expects to spend **more than $200 billion** and then close its doors for good on ==31 December 2045==. His reason fits in one line: "People will say a lot of things about me when I die," but __he is determined that "he died rich" will not be one of them__.

glance.label: Grew up
glance.value: Seattle, the second of three children. Father William H. Gates Sr. was a lawyer and civic leader; mother Mary Gates was a schoolteacher, University of Washington regent and chair of United Way International

glance.label: First computer
glance.value: Lakeside School in Seattle, where a new computer terminal hooked him at about 12 or 13, in eighth grade

glance.label: Education
glance.value: Entered Harvard in 1973 to study mathematics; left in 1975 to build a business with Paul Allen; came back for an honorary degree in 2007

glance.label: First paid work
glance.value: At about 15 he and school friends were paid to write Lakeside's class-scheduling program; an earlier payroll program for a Portland company paid them in free computer time, not money

glance.label: First company (age)
glance.value: Microsoft, co-founded with Paul Allen in 1975, when Gates was 19; based in Albuquerque, New Mexico, until it moved to Washington state

glance.label: Leaving Microsoft
glance.value: Stopped day-to-day work in June 2008, stepped down as chairman in February 2014 and left the board in March 2020

glance.label: Today
glance.value: Chair of the Gates Foundation, which he and Melinda French Gates set up in 2000; founder of Breakthrough Energy; runs his private office, Gates Ventures; chairman of the nuclear company TerraPower; co-founded the Giving Pledge in 2010

glance.label: Fortune
glance.value: About $118.2 billion (Forbes, 29 Oct 2026, world #16), made from Microsoft; Forbes estimates he now owns less than 1% of it after giving more than $63.9 billion to his foundation

glance.label: Family and home
glance.value: Three children and two grandchildren; he and Melinda French Gates announced their divorce in 2021 after 27 years of marriage; lives in Medina, Washington, USA

contact.howToReach: Bill Gates has no public personal email or phone, so every real route runs through his organisations, and none of them hands out money to individuals. If you work at a non-profit, university or startup in global health, farming, sanitation or education, the honest way in is the Gates Foundation's published Requests for Proposals; the foundation says it mostly invites proposals itself and will not review pitches sent through its general contact form. Journalists should use the foundation's media line or email, or the press contacts of Microsoft and TerraPower; shareholders should use Microsoft Investor Relations. To hear what he is thinking, follow Gates Notes and his verified LinkedIn, X and Instagram accounts, where he posts about books, AI, health and climate. Never pay a 'grant fee' or share bank details with anyone promising Gates money: the foundation says it never asks for these, and you can check a suspicious message by forwarding it to phishing@gatesfoundation.org.

factCheck.method: Front matter and contact card built from primary and established sources only, read live on 29 Oct 2026: the Gates Foundation's own pages (contact, write-to-us, scam-reporting and grant FAQ pages, fact sheet, leadership bio, Delhi office page and Bill Gates's 8 May 2025 essay; obfuscated emails decoded from the live page), the German Bundestag lobbying register (a government record) for the foundation's mailing address, SEC EDGAR company data for Microsoft's address and phone, Microsoft's Investor Relations page and FY2026 Q4 earnings release, Microsoft's March 2020 board announcement and 'Microsoft at 50' page, TerraPower's about and contact pages, Forbes' real-time profile (29 Oct 2026), the Academy of Achievement biography and interview, the Harvard Gazette transcript of his 2007 commencement speech, and the Computer History Museum. Socials are listed only when linked from the Gates Foundation's own pages or shown as verified on the platform. Photos come from Wikimedia Commons via the Commons API, with author, licence and description copied from the file page. Dropped: the YouTube handle 'thisisbillgates', which resolves to an unrelated channel named 'Ray', so no personal YouTube or Threads account is listed; the Gates Foundation's Seattle street address, because its own contact pages publish no street address; Breakthrough Energy contact details, because its site publishes none.

disputed.note: Forbes, the Gates Foundation and Microsoft's own 'Microsoft at 50' page date the founding to 1975. The Academy of Achievement biography says Gates and Allen started Microsoft in 1976 after moving to New Mexico; Microsoft says the company was based in Albuquerque from 1976 to 1978. We use 1975.

disputed.claim: Gates first used a computer at Lakeside at age 13.
disputed.note: The Academy of Achievement biography says he was about 13 when Lakeside got its terminal; in his own interview on the same site he says he was 12, in eighth grade. We say 'about 12 or 13'.
TerraPower's own site says Gates has been its chairman since 2006, while a leadership bio on the same site says the company was founded in 2008. We give no founding year.
